builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
summary: SPILLWAY replaces per-task LLM-based planning or routing for security with a deterministic admission check that validates tool-call targets against typed fields from read-only tools, plus a rule-based sanitizer that strips instruction-like regions before the model sees them. It costs implementation complexity: defining typed tool schemas, fixed delegation rules, sanitizer patterns, and an optional local judge, but adds almost no model-call overhead or latency. It can fail if attacks evade the fixed sanitizer rules, if delegation rules are misconfigured, or if legitimate targets are refused and the local judge errs, and it only defends against target-redirection, not other attack classes like data exfiltration through allowed targets.
rationale: The method is directly applicable to constrained infrastructure since it requires no extra model calls and no clusters, but adopting it requires engineering effort to define typed schemas, delegation rules, and sanitizer patterns specific to the reader's tool ecosystem, so it warrants a small-scale pilot before full production commitment.
technique: Deterministic tool-target admission control with sanitization

claims.statement: SPILLWAY replaces per-task LLM-based planning or routing for security with a deterministic admission check that validates tool-call targets against typed fields from read-only tools, plus a rule-based sanitizer that strips instruction-like regions before the model sees them. It costs implementation complexity: defining typed tool schemas, fixed delegation rules, sanitizer patterns, and an optional local judge, but adds almost no model-call overhead or latency. It can fail if attacks evade the fixed sanitizer rules, if delegation rules are misconfigured, or if legitimate targets are refused and the local judge errs, and it only defends against target-redirection, not other attack classes like data exfiltration through allowed targets.
Achieves defense with no defense-triggered backbone re-run and almost no added model calls; attack success under released RL attacker is .007.
